thread:
ana: heads up — seeing a micro-slot stasis pattern in ap-se1 (apse1-b/apse1-c). lots of tiny GPU pods pending, eviction_count on warmpool nodes jumped. anybody oncall?
sam: I see the alert. ops-bot posted a spike ~2m ago. quick grep shows pending pods are 0.125/0.25GPU tiny-workers stuck for attach.
ops-bot: ALERT: scheduler.preempt_evictions_rate > 90/s in apse1c for last 3m.
mike: link to prometheus panels?
sam: https://dash/repl?panel=slot_stasis&range=15m — pending pods clusters: apse1-b/c, node groups warm-*
nana: I meant to ping emily :)
emily: on it, paging infra. initial hunch: connect/attach latency to warmpool init causing latebind + preempt thrash.
lee: also seeing AZ fairness metric degrading — apse1-b has 70% of tiny pod allocations while apse1-c starves.
sam: can we get a node-level log excerpt?
emily: grabbing from node gpu-warm-37: ```May 12 12:02:17 kubelet[1]: attach failed: rpc timeout (attach: nvlink-attach 120s)
May 12 12:03:54 kubelet[1]: eviction: pod tiny-worker-7 forced by scheduler preempt
May 12 12:03:55 kubelet[1]: attach succeeded after 150s```
mike: 150s attach = catastrophic for tiny pods. explains preempt loop.
nana: what's changed recently? warmpool image? kubelet upgrade?
emily: we rolled kernel patch to 5.10.89 on warm nodes 2 hours ago (auto-roll).
lee: cross-check: nodes with kernel 5.10.89 have attach latency 60-200s; older kernel nodes ~2-4s.
sam: ops plan: revert kernel on warmpool nodes in apse1-b/c or mark them unschedulable for tiny pods. prefer quick revert.
emily: can also adjust scheduler policy: increase gang packing window for tiny pods from 5s -> 30s to reduce attach contention. but that's medium-risk.
mike: revert first. pushing a node pool rollback on apse1-b/c (small batch). tagging oncall-alert.
ops-bot: DEPLOY: rollout started for nodepool warm-apse1 (rollback) — https://ci/deploy/789
sam: also set taint temporary: `kubectl taint nodes warm-apse1-* tiny-batch=true:NoSchedule` to stop new tiny pods hitting them while rollback proceeds. :thumbsup:
emily: doing that now.
nana: what about evictions tally? we should suppress alert noise, add transient alert mute 15m.
lee: agreed — muting preempt_evictions_rate for apse1 namespace 15m.
ops-bot: ALERT MUTE: preempt_evictions_rate (apse1) 15m by emily
mike: after rollback finishes, run a packing sim to verify attach latency restored. I can run quick test job: `kubectl run tiny-job --image=busybox --requests='100m/0.125GPU' --replicas=200`
sam: good. add a retention note: open ticket to track kernel rollback vs nic driver mismatch; could be upstream CVE patch interaction.
emily: created ticket INFRA-4821 with logs and timeline.
nana: follow-up: consider scheduler fix — prefer short-lived pods to warm nodes with low attach-latency tag. add to roadmap.
lee: also check cloud provider attach API quotas — if kernel increased retransmits we may hit quota.
mike: test job starting now, will post results in 5m.
ops-bot: DEPLOY COMPLETE: nodepool warm-apse1 rollback finished (30/30).
emily: removing taint on healthy nodes.
sam: test job status?
mike: 200 replicas scheduled, 196 running within 40s, no evictions. attach latency median 3.2s.
nana: awesome. closing immediate incident. any longer term actions? list: 1) investigate kernel/driver interaction (INFRA-4821) 2) scheduler affinity tag for low-attach nodes 3) warmpool rollout gating and canary 4) tweak eviction alert thresholds for tiny-pod patterns.
emily: I'll own #1 and #3. sam can lead #2. mike owns #4.
lee: adding notes to runbook: "micro-slot stasis" troubleshooting checklist (attach latencies, node kernel, taint/warmpool gating).
sam: thanks all. :tada:
nana: ping if anything regresses.
